evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Lingjiao Chen, Matei Zaharia and James Zou
evidence_items.explanation: This supports the regression component for particular service behaviors. The same abstract reports improvements on other tasks, so it does not establish a general decline or a slowing rate of improvement.

evidence_items.locator: Tracking Performance of Proprietary APIs - GPT-4-0314 vs 0613?
evidence_items.explanation: Users preferred the earlier GPT-4 version, supporting a local service regression. The authors also identify changing users and comparison sets as possible explanations; their table places GPT-4 Turbo above the June version.

evidence_items.locator: Full Leaderboard with GPT-4-Turbo as judge, explanatory paragraph and following table
evidence_items.explanation: The table scores April GPT-4 Turbo at 82.6 against 50.0 for the March 2023 baseline, showing improvement on this evaluation. The authors warn about model-judge bias; these comparisons do not measure whether progress was slowing.

unresolved_gaps: No representative, consistently measured time series establishes a declining rate of improvement through April 2024.
The speaker supplies no rule for combining task-specific gains and losses into an overall trend.
API-version comparisons do not capture every change in the ChatGPT service.
